Definition: of uncertain derivation; to cheat, i.e. delude:--deceive.
BiblicalUsage: To cheat or delude — Eve was deceived, Paul says, and Adam was not; empty words deceive the sons of disobedience; and a man who thinks himself religious while his tongue runs loose deceives his own heart. Deception always works the same way: it promises something and delivers nothing.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe deception is the oldest trick in the book, and it still starts with a lie about God's word. The guard against it is simple and hard: listen to what God actually said, and let it judge my heart before my heart judges it.
